THREE FINDINGS MEASURED DURING REVISION that materially change the delegated premises: (1) the working tree has REVERTED all of Phases 1-5's code as an uncommitted 43+/357- diff against HEAD, removing the entire --legacy-schema mode and all four doc_id fallback branches -- Phase 6.1 now restores it from HEAD behind a mandatory git-snapshot.sh --no-revert, since git checkout on a dirty tree is guard-blocked; (2) the Phase 1 fix is now a functional no-op (map-diff old 127 / new 127, added []) and the legacy gate matches 0 of 321 entries because the migration gave every former legacy entry a sources/-prefixed path -- so a --legacy-schema re-run cannot re-adjudicate arisaka, which has itself migrated to the sources/ schema and needs default mode instead; (3) arisaka will NOT be rescued by a re-run -- measured pdftotext 19,439 words vs whole-doc md 10,007 (ratio 0.5148) and chunk-sum 9,968 (ratio 0.5128), both far below the 0.75 threshold, so the plan states a quarantined outcome as the expected honest result and forbids threshold adjustment. HEAD (335c034a) has the work; the working tree does not. The revert is uncommitted and unexplained by any commit message. Phase 6.1 restores from HEAD behind a mandatory 'bash .claude/scripts/git-snapshot.sh 555 --no-revert', because git checkout -- <path> on a dirty tree is forbidden by .claude/rules/git-workflow.md and blocked by guard-destructive-git.sh. Restoring is the conservative default (HEAD is the committed record and the snapshot makes it reversible); whether the code should ultimately be kept or retired as dead code is surfaced in the Phase 7 memo, not decided.

Disposition of the sourceless documents remains a genuine user decision, and its polarity has reversed. no_source_pdf is NOT on QUARANTINED_FIDELITY_VALUES, so all 66 documents stamped with it are already returned by default no-flag search, non-degraded and unannounced -- option (c)'s effect is de facto live. Option (d) 'leave as-is' now means CITABLE, not quarantined. Option (b) is now a rollback of live behavior, not a no-op. Phase 7 writes this up as a memo; it does not resolve it. No repository code caused this state: no_source_pdf was always in the audit script's six-value enum, the quarantine constant was never edited, and the stamping came from the Literature repo's commit bb3bf18.

The Phase 1 doc_id fallback adds zero keys against the current index.json (map-diff harness: old 127 / new 127, added []) and the --legacy-schema gate matches 0 of 321 entries, because the Literature migration gave every former legacy entry a sources/-prefixed path. The Phase 1-5 work is correct and unchanged; the corpus moved underneath it. Phase 7 puts the keep-or-retire question to the user without answering it.

arisakadasstrassburger_2015 has migrated to the sources/ schema (path and id now present), so the delegated '--legacy-schema re-run' cannot reach it -- default mode applies instead. The re-run is mechanical but will NOT rescue it: measured pdftotext 19,439 words vs whole-document md 10,007 (ratio 0.5148) and chunk-sum 9,968 (ratio 0.5128), both far below RATIO_THRESHOLD 0.75 and consistent with the stored 0.539. The markdown genuinely contains about half the source's words. The plan states a quarantined outcome as the expected honest result and forbids adjusting RATIO_THRESHOLD or PROOF_ADEQUACY_THRESHOLD. Only the disclosure/proof-completeness escape path could change the verdict, and the plan requires measuring it rather than predicting it. If the user wants this document citable, re-converting the source is the honest route, not re-adjudication.
